source_title: Bihar Politics: Supreme Court Setback for Anant Singh in Dularchand Yadav Murder Case, Must Surrender by December 1!
source_excerpt:
Former Bihar MLA and JD(U) leader Anant Singh has suffered a major setback in the Dularchand Yadav murder case after the Supreme Court directed him to surrender by December 1. The court's order means that Anant Singh will have to return to jail while the legal proceedings in the case continue. Reacting to the Supreme Court's decision, Anant Singh said that he has faith in the judiciary and will surrender as directed. However, he also indicated that he would approach the court again through a fresh appeal. Anant Singh accused JD(U) leader Neeraj Kumar of framing him in the murder case and alleged that political conspiracy was behind the action against him. While speaking about the incident, Anant Singh claimed that he and his supporters were campaigning during the election when they encountered Dularchand Yadav on the road. According to his version, an argument and subsequent clash took place between the groups. He alleged that Dularchand Yadav was deliberately targeted and that he was falsely implicated in the case following the incident. Anant Singh further made allegations against Neeraj Kumar, claiming that several legal cases against him were connected to the latter's political influence. He maintained that he had entered electoral politics without such cases against him and blamed his political rivals for his current legal troubles. The Supreme Court's direction to surrender by December 1 has once again brought the Dularchand Yadav murder case into the political spotlight in Bihar. Anant Singh's reaction has also intensified the political exchange, with his allegations against Neeraj Kumar adding another dimension to the controversy. The case remains significant for Bihar politics as attention now turns to Anant Singh's surrender and his next legal move.
